settings.heading: Most wet feet are not earned on a mountain.
settings.lede: A dog walk across wet grass, the school run, twenty minutes to the station and back. Ordinary trainers are not waterproof, and nobody buys hiking boots to walk to work.

settings.heading: The gap nobody buys footwear for.
settings.lede: There is a whole category of wet feet that no one treats as a kit problem, because the obvious fix — owning waterproof shoes for the walk to the shops — is absurd. So the shoes stay wrong and the feet stay wet.

settings.title: Grass holds more water than rain does
settings.body: Twenty minutes across a wet field in mesh trainers soaks a foot more thoroughly than an hour of walking in drizzle.

settings.title: Trainers are built to breathe, not to seal
settings.body: The mesh that stops your feet cooking in July is an open door in November. It is doing exactly what it was designed to do.

settings.title: It is the same pair every day
settings.body: A hill walker's boots get a day off to dry out. The shoes you wear every morning do not.

settings.heading: The layer that moves between shoes.
settings.head_note: You wear them under the trainers, shoes or boots you already own. The waterproofing travels with your feet rather than living in one pair of footwear.

settings.title: It works in the shoes you have
settings.body: There is nothing to buy twice. The same pair goes under trainers on Monday and under boots on Saturday.

settings.title: Porelle®, named on the label
settings.body: A licensed third-party membrane rather than an unnamed laminate — the one specification in this category you can look up without taking our word for it.

settings.title: Crew height, unisex sizing
settings.body: One height, sized in bands rather than by gender, so a household can share a size between them.

settings.heading: The same pair, in the conditions this page is about.
settings.head_note: Product imagery rather than a documentary shoot, so read it for what the sock is and where it goes — not as evidence. The checkable claim is the membrane.

settings.title: They are not a winter-only sock
settings.body: Because the membrane breathes, they are wearable when it is not raining. Plenty of people wear them as their normal sock and stop checking the forecast.

settings.title: Two pairs is the honest number
settings.body: One on, one in the wash. Anything beyond that is preference, not requirement.

settings.title: Cool wash, no conditioner, no dryer
settings.body: The same care as any technical layer. Fabric conditioner coats a membrane and heat is what finishes one off.

settings.heading: What it will not fix.
settings.body: If your shoes are wrong for the ground, this does not repair that. A soaked trainer around a dry foot is still a soaked trainer — heavier, colder, and no quicker to dry by the door.
